Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required wake-visual inspection and fish-control bookshelf skills before touching the policy. I’ll keep the implementation to one candidate and verify both required documentation updates.

The visual-first skill requires a score/observation/metrics/image cross-check, and the bookshelf requires translating only normalized body-frame invariants. I’m now grounding the candidate in the inherited guidance and all sampled outcomes before proposing the architecture.

The sampled runs are all direct-uniform still-water episodes, so their motion is self-propelled. The inherited record points to two distinct failures—coherent but shallow route correction versus a closer turn with terminal carrier loss. I’m inspecting both visual rows and reducing the large diagnostics to the control signals needed to distinguish them.

A stronger semantic result appears in the assigned parent’s inherited log: phase-aligned steering preserved the carrier and reached `0.9532L`, much closer than every sampled solver but still outside the `0.75L` disk. This materially changes the next test: I’m treating that near-capture as the mechanism to refine, not reverting to mean curvature or carrier attenuation.

The near-capture’s terminal wake remains coherent and joint phase-plane energy stays near `0.8`; the failure is actuator realization, not propulsion loss. In the evidenced `14–20T`, `<4L` regime, reconstruction shows only about `27%` (head) and `31%` (tail) of the intended carrier-aligned steering increment survives the hard acceleration clamp. I’ll record that diagnosis before replacing acceleration-aligned pulses with joint-motion-aligned duty steering.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The new lesson captures the parent’s near-capture and the clamp-erased steering budget, while the policy changes only the terminal phase observable. I’m invoking the workspace’s required check runner now and will repair any contract failures it finds; no CFD will be run.

The first required check exposed a workspace metadata defect before evaluating our edits: `README.md` marks the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker reports two copied examples instead of one. I’m inspecting the checker and will make the smallest in-scope repair needed to let the intended parent comparison run.

The guidance and editable-boundary checks pass. The check runner could not find Julia on `PATH`, but this host has a working Julia runtime outside `PATH`; I’m using it only for the prescribed finite-action contract probe, still with no CFD.

All contract probes now pass: material guidance, editable boundary, finite two-joint action, parameter-schema ownership, reflection equivariance, and exact preservation of the assigned parent outside the `<4L` terminal gate. I’m doing a final artifact audit now; formal CFD remains deferred to EvE.

Produced exactly one candidate: motion-aligned terminal duty steering, preserving the inherited carrier and far-field behavior while shifting steering to joint-motion phases with actuator headroom.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

All required checks pass: guidance materiality, solver boundary, parameter schema, finite bounded actions, reflection equivariance, and exact parent behavior beyond `4L`. I also removed a duplicated assigned-parent marker in `README.md` that initially broke the guidance checker. No CFD was run.
